items.text: Rock: Dahl integration across units — We noticed the Dahl businesses keep separate brands and units; reconciling order and financial data across them may be manual (inferred from public announcement, not confirmed internally).
Rock: Deal completion conditions pending — European Commission approved the deal unconditionally, but completion still depends on other conditions, with completion targeted by end-2026.
Rock: Rights issue timing pressure — A €500-700m rights issue is proposed, with an EGM on 2026-10-30; terms not yet set, so post-deal spending timing is open.

Rock: Warehouse rollout across five sites — Manhattan Associates ActiveWarehouse initial rollout covers five distribution centres, with a new site in 2029-30; integration with existing workflows is an open question.

Lighthouse: Dahl order-data reconciliation tool — A scoped pilot could cut manual cross-unit reconciliation during integration, if that work exists; we would first ask the team to confirm where it happens.
Lighthouse: Warehouse-to-ERP workflow bridge — Adjacent to the Manhattan rollout, a connector for gaps between warehouse and finance systems could ship in weeks once requirements are confirmed.

Lighthouse: Tender-document intake automation — Public tender notices show Kesko winning many public lots; automating bid-data gathering could speed responses, pending confirmation of current process.

blocks.label: Captain's note (to the CEO)
blocks.text: We noticed Kesko's sails are set wide: the Dahl deal, a rights issue, and a €20bn horizon. Those waters hold hidden rocks in integration and data flow. We'd love to chart a route with your team, one buoy at a time, starting with a conversation about where manual work slows the crew down. Shall we plan the passage together?
Rocks are read from public evidence, not from inside the company. Chart is a conversation starter.
